meaning: busy; having a lot to do

senses.en: busy (of a person): 我很忙 'I'm busy'
busy, hectic (of work or a period): 工作很忙

examples.en: Are you busy right now?
examples.analysis: 忙 is the whole predicate: Chinese needs no 是 'to be' before an adjective. 现在 'right now' sits before it. This is a polite opener before asking someone for a minute of their time.

examples.en: I'm too busy today. How about tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 太 + 忙 + 了 = 'too busy': 太…了 frames the adjective. 明天吧 is a short counter-offer, a time + 吧 meaning 'let's make it tomorrow'. A soft way to turn down a plan for today.

examples.en: I'm not busy. Go ahead.
examples.analysis: 不 + 忙 = 'not busy'. As a reply to 你忙吗, the subject 我 drops out. 你说吧 'go ahead (and say it)' invites the other person to start talking.

related.en: to help; to do someone a favor

hook: 忄 on the left is 心 'heart' squeezed to the side; 亡 (wáng) on the right hints at the sound (both end in -ang). 忘 'to forget' has the same two parts stacked.

meaning: house; home (a house or a flat as a building or property)

senses.en: house, flat or apartment: the home as a building or property

measure.note: 一套房子 'a flat / apartment (one unit)'; a whole house or building is 一栋房子 or 一座房子; casual speech also says 一个房子

examples.en: Their place is really big!
examples.analysis: 房子 is the subject; 真 + adjective is an exclamation, 'really …!'. 房子 covers a flat as well as a house, so English 'place' often fits better than 'house'.

examples.zh: 你们在北京买房子了吗？
examples.en: Have you bought a place in Beijing?
examples.analysis: 买房子 'buy a home' is a common small-talk topic in China. 在北京 comes before the verb to give the place. 了 + 吗 asks whether it has happened yet.

examples.zh: 这房子太老了，我不想住。
examples.en: This place is too old. I don't want to live here.
examples.analysis: In speech 这 can go straight onto a noun with no measure word: 这房子. 老 'old' works for buildings too. 不想住 'don't want to live (in it)': the place is understood, so no object follows 住.

related.en: home; family (where you live and the people, not the building as property)

hook: 房 = 户 'door' (the top part) + 方 (fāng), which gives the sound.

meaning: clothes; clothing (one garment or clothes in general)

senses.en: clothes; a garment (a top, a jacket, an outfit)

measure.note: 一件衣服 'a piece of clothing' (a shirt, a jacket); 套 for a suit or set

examples.en: I'm going to do the laundry.
examples.analysis: 洗衣服 'wash clothes' is the everyday way to say 'do the laundry'. 去 + verb = 'go and do it'. 衣服 here means clothes in general, with no number.

examples.zh: 外边很冷，多穿一点儿衣服。
examples.en: It's cold outside, so put on a few more layers.
examples.analysis: 多 + verb = 'do more of it': 多穿 'wear more'. 一点儿 'a bit' sits between the verb and 衣服. A typical caring line from a parent or partner; the 'you' is dropped, as in English commands.

examples.zh: 你的衣服真好看，在哪儿买的？
examples.en: Your outfit is really nice. Where did you buy it?
examples.analysis: 衣服 is the subject of 真好看 'really good-looking'. It can mean one item or the whole outfit; English picks 'top', 'jacket' or 'outfit' from context. 在哪儿买的 with 的 at the end asks about a detail of a past purchase.

collocations.en: to buy clothes; go clothes shopping

related.en: to wear; to put on (clothes, shoes)

meaning: to sleep; to go to bed

senses.en: to sleep; to go to bed (睡了 'has gone to bed')
with a time or result after it: 睡一会儿 'take a nap', 睡好 'sleep well'

examples.en: Are you asleep?
examples.analysis: 睡 + 了 + 吗 asks whether it has already happened: 'have you gone to sleep?'. A classic late-night text before asking something, or a check on a family member.

examples.en: I want to sleep for a bit.
examples.analysis: 一会儿 'a little while' goes right after 睡 to say how long. With 睡觉 the time goes in the middle instead: 睡一会儿觉. 想 + verb = 'want to, would like to'.

examples.en: I didn't sleep well last night.
examples.analysis: 睡好 = sleep + 好 'well, properly', a result after the verb. 没 negates it because this is about what happened last night. The time phrase can come before the subject, as here.

collocations.en: to sleep; to go to bed

related.en: to sleep; the usual word for 'go to bed'

hook: 目 'eye' on the left, 垂 'to droop' on the right: drooping eyelids.

meaning: to go back (to where you came from, away from here)

senses.en: to go back, return (home, to your office, to your country)
back there: 走回去 'walk back', 拿回去 'take back with you'

examples.en: I'll head back now.
examples.analysis: A standard line for leaving a dinner, a party or the office (我先走了 is just as common). 先 'first, before the others' softens it: you leave, they stay. 了 marks the change that is about to happen: 'I'm off now'.

examples.en: What date are you going back?
examples.analysis: 回去 means going back to where you came from or are based (home, your hotel, your city, your country), seen from where you are now. 几号 'what date' (day of the month) comes before the verb.

examples.zh: 太晚了，我们打车回去吧。
examples.en: It's really late. Let's take a taxi back.
examples.analysis: Two verbs in a row: 打车 says how you go, 回去 says where to, 'back'. 吧 turns it into a suggestion, 'let's'. 太晚了 here just means 'it's very late', not a complaint.

collocations.en: go on back; you can go now
to take it back with you

meaning: late (after the usual or agreed time; late in the day)

senses.en: late, after the expected time: 来晚了 'came late'
late in the day or night: 太晚了 'it's late'

examples.en: Sorry I'm late.
examples.analysis: 来晚了 = come + late + 了: 晚 follows the verb as its result, 'arrived late'. This is a standard apology when you turn up late; 我迟到了 'I'm late' is the other common one. Here Chinese attaches 'late' to the action 来.

examples.zh: 还不晚，我们再坐一会儿吧。
examples.en: It's not late yet. Let's stay a little longer.
examples.analysis: 还不晚 'not late yet': 还 + 不 = 'still not'. 晚 describes the time itself, so there is no subject. 再坐一会儿 'sit a while longer' is how you say 'stay a bit more' at a friend's place.

examples.en: He often gets home late.
examples.analysis: Here 很晚 comes before the verb and gives the time: 'at a late hour'. Compare 来晚了, where 晚 after the verb means 'later than expected'. 常常 'often' comes before the whole verb phrase.

meaning: broken; gone bad; bad; (after a feeling) extremely

senses.en: broken, not working; (of food) gone off: 手机坏了
bad (of people, news, habits)
extremely, after a feeling: 饿坏了 'starving'

examples.en: My phone's broken.
examples.analysis: 坏 + 了 = 'has broken, is broken now': 了 marks the change from working to not working. Use it for anything that stops working: a phone, a car, a door, a computer.

examples.en: This meat has gone off, hasn't it? Don't eat it.
examples.analysis: For food, 坏了 means 'has gone bad'. 吧 at the end of a statement asks the listener to agree: '…, hasn't it?'. 别 + verb + 了 tells someone to stop or not go ahead.

examples.en: I'm starving!
examples.analysis: After a feeling word, 坏了 means 'terribly, to the limit': 饿坏了 'starving', 累坏了 'worn out'. Nothing is broken here; it is a strong, informal way to say how you feel.

related.en: good; (after a verb) done properly: 修好 'fixed'

meaning: water

senses.en: water (to drink, to wash with, from the tap)

measure.note: 一杯水 'a glass of water'; 一瓶水 'a bottle of water'

examples.en: Could I have a glass of water, please?
examples.analysis: 一杯水 = number + container word 杯 + noun: to count water you name what it comes in. 请给我 + thing is a polite way to ask for something in a restaurant, a shop or an office.

examples.en: No tea for me. Water's fine.
examples.analysis: 水就行 'water will do': 就行 means 'that's enough, that works'. 不喝 here declines what is being offered now. A polite way to refuse tea or a drink and ask for water instead.

examples.zh: 水太热了，等一会儿再喝。
examples.en: The water's too hot. Wait a bit before you drink it.
examples.analysis: 水 is the subject of 太热了 'too hot'. 等一会儿再喝 'wait a while, then drink': 再 here means 'and only then', not 'again'. For a drink too hot to sip, people often say 烫 'scalding' instead of 热.

meaning: measure word for drinks: a cup of, a glass of

senses.en: a cup / glass of (a drink): 一杯茶, 两杯水
stands for the drink itself after 这/那 or a number: 这杯 'this one'

examples.en: I'd like two cups of tea.
examples.analysis: Number + 杯 + drink. Before a measure word, 'two' on its own is normally 两, not 二 (but 十二杯 'twelve cups'). 我要 'I'll have' is the normal way to order in a café or restaurant.

examples.en: Come on, have a drink!
examples.analysis: No drink is named: 喝一杯 'have a drink' often means a drink of beer or wine with friends, like the English phrase. 来 at the start means 'come on', an invitation.

examples.en: Whose drink is this?
examples.analysis: 这 + 杯 = 'this cup (of drink)': the measure word follows 这 and the noun drops out. It points at a cup with a drink in it; for the cup as an object, people say 杯子.

related.en: the general measure word; 杯 is for drinks

meaning: school (any level, including a university)

senses.en: school; also a university, from a student's or staff member's point of view

measure.note: 一所学校 in careful speech; 一个学校 in everyday talk

examples.en: Is the kids' school far?
examples.analysis: 学校 is the subject; 远不远 'far or not far' is a yes/no question made by repeating the adjective with 不 between. 孩子的学校 'the kids' school' (孩子 can be one child or several): 的 links owner and thing.

examples.zh: 我们学校有很多外国学生。
examples.en: Our school has a lot of foreign students.
examples.analysis: 我们学校 'our school' needs no 的: 我们 + a group or institution you belong to can link directly (我们的学校 is also correct). University students and staff also call their university 学校. 有 'has, there are'.

examples.en: There's nobody at the school on Sundays.
examples.analysis: 学校里 'in the school': 里 after a place noun means 'inside, on the grounds'. 没有人 'there is nobody'. The time 星期天 comes first, then the place.

related.en: to go to school; to be at school

meaning: tall; high

senses.en: tall (people, trees, buildings)
high (prices, levels, standards)

examples.en: The buildings here are so tall!
examples.analysis: 高 is the predicate, with no 是 before it. 真 + adjective is an exclamation, 'so …!'. 这儿的楼 'the buildings here': 的 links the place to the thing.

examples.en: How tall are you?
examples.analysis: 多 + a size adjective asks 'how …?': 多高 'how tall', 多远 'how far'. The answer usually comes in meters: 一米八 'one meter eighty'.

examples.en: He's taller than me.
examples.analysis: A + 比 + B + adjective = 'A is more … than B'; 高 alone becomes 'taller'. No 很 goes here; to say 'much taller', add 多了 after it: 他比我高多了.

related.en: short (in height): 他很矮; never 他很低

meaning: movie; film

senses.en: movie; film

measure.note: 一部电影 'a movie'; casual speech often says 一个电影

examples.en: Let's go see a movie tonight!
examples.analysis: 看电影 'see a movie': Chinese uses 看 'look, watch' for films. 一起去 'go together'; 吧 turns it into a suggestion, 'let's'. 晚上 at the front sets the time, 'this evening'.

examples.en: Is this movie any good?
examples.analysis: 好看 'good to watch' is a common way to ask if a movie is good; for food the word is 好吃. 这个电影: 这 + measure word + noun. 吗 makes the yes/no question.

examples.en: I've already seen that movie.
examples.analysis: The object 那个电影 moves to the front as the topic: 'that movie, I've seen it'. 看过 = 'have seen (at some point)'; 了 at the end adds 'already'.

collocations.en: to watch a movie; go to the movies

meaning: to try; to try on, try out

senses.en: to try; to have a go (试试, 试一下儿)
to try on (clothes, shoes) or try out (a thing, a method)

examples.en: Can I try it?
examples.analysis: 试一下儿 'give it a try': 一下儿 after a verb makes the action short and casual. 能…吗 asks permission. In a clothes shop this means 'try it on'.

examples.en: I tried. It's too hard.
examples.analysis: 试 + 了 = 'tried (it)', a finished attempt. The second half gives the result: 太难了 'too difficult'. No object is needed when both sides know what was tried.

examples.en: Give it another try.
examples.analysis: 试试 = the verb said twice, a light 'have a go'. 再 'again' + 吧 turns it into encouragement after a failed attempt. In speech the second 试 is said lightly.

meaning: on (your) body; on you (what you are carrying or wearing)

senses.en: on you: what you are carrying right now (身上没钱)
on or over the body (身上很热 'my body feels hot')

examples.en: I don't have any money on me.
examples.analysis: 身上 'on (my) person' means what you are carrying right now. Person + 身上 + 没有 + thing = 'have no … on me'. It says nothing about money at home or in the bank.

examples.zh: 我身上很热，是不是生病了？
examples.en: I feel hot. Am I getting sick?
examples.analysis: Here 身上 is the whole body: 身上很热 'my body feels hot'. 是不是 + statement asks 'could it be that…?', and 生病了 'have fallen ill'.

examples.en: It's raining, and I'm all wet.
examples.analysis: 身上都是水 'water all over me': 都是 here means 'is all, is covered with'. 下雨了 'it has started raining': 了 marks the new situation.

meaning: room (in a home, hotel or office)

senses.en: room (a bedroom, a hotel room, an office room)

measure.note: 一个房间 in everyday speech; with 间 people usually say 房 alone: 一间房, 两间房

examples.en: My room is upstairs.
examples.analysis: 在 + place = 'is (located) at': 房间在楼上 'the room is upstairs'. No 是 is needed to say where something is.

examples.en: Do you have any rooms left?
examples.analysis: At a hotel, 有房间吗 asks whether a room is free. 还 'still' adds 'left, still available'. 你们 'you (plural)' addresses the hotel, not just the person at the desk.

examples.en: Don't go into my room!
examples.analysis: 别 + verb = 'don't'. 进 'enter' takes the room directly as its object; no word for 'into' is needed. 我房间 'my room': in speech 的 often drops between a pronoun and a familiar place.

hook: 房 = 户 'door' (the top part) + 方 (fāng), which gives the sound.

meaning: book

senses.en: book

examples.en: What book are you reading?
examples.analysis: In everyday speech, reading a book is 看书. 读书 can also mean 'read books' (我爱读书), but it often means 'study, be in school' (他在北京读书). 在 + verb = '-ing' right now. 什么书 'what book' sits in the object slot, where the answer would go.

examples.en: This book is really good.
examples.analysis: 这 + 本 + 书: 本 is the measure word for books, between 这 and the noun. 好看 'good to look at' also means 'a good read' for a book.

examples.en: None of these books are mine.
examples.analysis: 都不 = 'none of them' (all + not). The order matters: 不都是 would mean 'not all of them'. 这些 'these' needs no measure word before 书. 我的 'mine': the noun drops after 的.

collocations.en: to read books; to study, be in school

meaning: ball; ball game, match

senses.en: ball (the object)
ball game; a match (打球 'play ball', 昨天的球 'yesterday's game')

measure.note: 一个球 'a ball'; 场 for a game: 一场球

examples.en: Did you watch the game yesterday?
examples.analysis: Here 球 means 'a match': 昨天的球 'yesterday's game'. It moves to the front as the topic, then 你看了吗 'did you watch it?'. Which sport is meant comes from context, often soccer or basketball.

examples.en: We played ball for two hours.
examples.analysis: 打球 'play ball' (basketball, badminton, table tennis…) is a verb + object, so the length of time goes between them: 打 + 了 + 两个小时 + 球. 打球打了两个小时 (verb said twice) is the other common order.

examples.en: The kids are playing with a ball outside.
examples.analysis: 玩儿球 'play with a ball' is casual play. For most ball sports the usual phrase is 打球 (basketball, badminton, table tennis…), but soccer is 踢球 'kick ball'. 在外边 'outside' comes before the verb. 孩子 can be one child or several; the plural marker 们 is optional.

related.en: to play a ball game (basketball, tennis…; soccer is 踢球)

hook: 王 on the left is really 玉 'jade' (a gem); 求 (qiú) on the right gives the exact sound.

meaning: to forget

senses.en: to forget (a name, a thing, to do something); usually 忘了

examples.en: I've forgotten his name.
examples.analysis: The object 他的名字 moves to the front as the topic: 'his name, I've forgotten it'. 忘了 closes the sentence with nothing after it. In speech 忘 usually comes with 了.

examples.en: I forgot to call him.
examples.analysis: 忘了 + an action = 'forgot to do it': the whole phrase 给他打电话 'call him' is what was forgotten. 给他 'to him' comes before the verb 打电话.

examples.en: Don't forget tomorrow's exam!
examples.analysis: 别忘了 + thing = 'don't forget …', a fixed reminder. 了 here does not report a past event; 别忘了 is simply the usual shape of the warning. 明天的考试 'tomorrow's exam'.

related.en: to forget; a little more formal than 忘了, but common in speech too
to remember (it) firmly; to keep in mind

hook: 亡 (wáng) on top gives the sound; 心 'heart, mind' below gives the meaning. 忙 'busy' has the same two parts side by side.

meaning: to come in (toward the speaker, who is inside)

senses.en: to come in (toward the speaker)
in, toward here: 走进来 'walk in', 拿进来 'bring in'

examples.en: Come on in!
examples.analysis: 进来 = 进 'enter' + 来 'toward here': you say it from inside, to someone at the door. 吧 makes it a warm invitation. 请进 is the set phrase for the same thing.

examples.en: How did you get in?
examples.analysis: 怎么 + verb + 的 asks how something already happened. 进来 again means coming in toward the speaker: the speaker is inside and surprised to see you there.

examples.en: He didn't come in. He's waiting at the door.
examples.analysis: 没 + 进来 = 'didn't come in'. The speaker is inside, so 进来, not 进去. 在门口等着 'waiting at the door': 着 marks an ongoing state.

related.en: to go in (away from the speaker)

meaning: road; the way; (measure word) bus route number

senses.en: road; street; path (一条路)
the way; the route or distance (认识路 'know the way')
route number for buses: 三路车 'the No. 3 bus'

examples.en: Which bus do I take to the airport?
examples.analysis: Here 路 is a measure word for bus routes: 几路车 'which number bus' (literally 'route how-many bus'). The answer is a number: 三路. 去机场 'to go to the airport' states the goal first.

examples.en: I don't know the way.
examples.analysis: 认识 'know, recognize' works for routes as well as people and characters: 认识路 'know the way'. 不认识路 means you don't know how to get there.

examples.en: Let's walk. It's not far.
examples.analysis: The second 路 is the subject: 路不远 'the way isn't far', i.e. 'it's not far'. 走路去 'go on foot', and 吧 makes it 'let's'.

collocations.en: to walk; to go on foot

related.en: on the way; on the road
